title: Klio
description: Backup and WAL observability for Klio, built from the Prometheus export of Klio's OpenTelemetry metrics.

panels.title: Backups in progress
panels.description: Base backups currently running across the plugin sidecars in the namespace.

panels.title: Time since last successful backup
panels.description: Elapsed time since the most recent base backup completed successfully. A value well above the backup interval means backups have stopped succeeding.

panels.title: Time since last failed backup
panels.description: Elapsed time since the most recent base backup failure. A small value means a failure happened recently.

panels.title: Latest backup duration
panels.description: Wall-clock duration of the most recent base backup.

panels.title: Time since last backup started
panels.description: Elapsed time since the most recent base backup started. Compare against the latest duration to tell whether a backup is still running or overdue.

panels.title: Backup success ratio
panels.description: Fraction of base backup runs that succeeded over the selected time range (successful runs / total runs).

panels.title: Successful backups (24h)
panels.description: Base backups that completed successfully in the last 24 hours. Counter resets on plugin restart make long-window counts approximate.

panels.title: Successful backups (7d)
panels.description: Base backups that completed successfully in the last 7 days. Counter resets on plugin restart make long-window counts approximate.

panels.title: Backup run rate by outcome
panels.description: Rate of base backup runs, broken down by outcome (success or failure).

panels.title: Backup failure rate by category
panels.description: Rate of failed base backup runs, broken down by failure category, to show why backups are failing.

panels.title: Backup duration (p50/p95/p99)
panels.description: Percentile wall-clock duration of base backup runs (across all outcomes), computed over the whole selected range so the lines stay populated between runs. Widen the dashboard range to span several backups for a stable reading; if the range contains no backup, the panel is empty.

panels.title: Backups by outcome
panels.description: Count of base backup runs per time bucket, split by outcome. Bars aggregate the number of backups over each interval (per day on a multi-day range).

panels.title: Streaming timeline by cluster
panels.description: PostgreSQL timeline the WAL streaming client is currently streaming, per cluster.

panels.title: WAL block send duration (p50/p95/p99) by cluster
panels.description: Percentile latency of the client's gRPC send of a WAL block to the server, per cluster. Most meaningful under active write load; on an idle or low-write cluster, WAL blocks are sent too infrequently for the underlying histogram_quantile to be reliable, so the line may look sparse or noisy rather than absent.

panels.title: WAL restore latency (p95) by cache hit
panels.description: 95th-percentile end-to-end WAL restore latency measured by the plugin: the latency PostgreSQL actually experiences, and in a replica cluster the speed of the replication path itself. cache_hit=true means the segment was already in the prefetch spool and the restore was a local rename; cache_hit=false means PostgreSQL had to wait on a download, so a falling hit ratio means prefetch is not keeping ahead of replay and the prefetch count may need raising. The two are orders of magnitude apart, hence the split rather than one pooled line.

panels.title: WAL restore hit ratio
panels.description: Fraction of WAL restores served directly from the prefetch spool instead of waiting on a download. A falling ratio means prefetch is not keeping pace with PostgreSQL replay.

panels.title: WAL restore rate by outcome
panels.description: Rate of WAL restore requests handled by the plugin, split by outcome (success or failure).

panels.title: Server uptime
panels.description: Time since the Klio server process started. A sudden drop means the server StatefulSet restarted.

panels.title: Latest WAL timeline by tier
panels.description: Current PostgreSQL timeline of the latest WAL written per tier. A change reflects a promotion or failover.

panels.title: Base snapshots by tier
panels.description: Base backup snapshots currently retained per tier.

panels.title: Latest snapshot size
panels.description: Size on the backend of the most recent base backup snapshot.

panels.title: Latest snapshot files
panels.description: Number of files in the most recent base backup snapshot.

panels.title: Latest snapshot dirs
panels.description: Number of directories in the most recent base backup snapshot.

panels.title: Latest snapshot age
panels.description: Age of the most recent base backup snapshot. Should stay below the backup interval.

panels.title: Oldest snapshot age
panels.description: Age of the oldest retained base backup snapshot, reflecting the effective retention horizon.

panels.title: Latest backup age (start)
panels.description: Elapsed time since the most recently retained PostgreSQL backup started.

panels.title: Latest backup age (completion)
panels.description: Elapsed time since the most recently retained PostgreSQL backup completed.

panels.title: Oldest backup age (start)
panels.description: Elapsed time since the oldest retained PostgreSQL backup started, reflecting the effective retention horizon.

panels.title: Oldest backup age (completion)
panels.description: Elapsed time since the oldest retained PostgreSQL backup completed, reflecting the effective retention horizon.

panels.title: PostgreSQL backups retained by tier
panels.description: Number of PostgreSQL backups currently retained per tier, across clusters.

panels.title: Latest backup LSN by cluster
panels.description: Start and end LSN of the latest retained PostgreSQL backup, per cluster.

panels.title: Oldest backup LSN by cluster
panels.description: Start and end LSN of the oldest retained PostgreSQL backup, per cluster.

panels.title: Backup timeline by cluster
panels.description: PostgreSQL timeline of the latest and oldest retained backup, per cluster. A mismatch means the retention window spans a promotion or failover.

panels.title: WAL files written rate by tier
panels.description: Rate of WAL files written by the server, split by storage tier.

panels.title: WAL bytes written rate by tier
panels.description: Rate of WAL bytes written by the server, split by storage tier.

panels.title: Time since last WAL written by tier
panels.description: Elapsed time since the server last wrote a WAL file for each tier. A stale tier-1 value means PostgreSQL stopped shipping WALs; a stale tier-2 value means the remote backend stopped receiving them.

panels.title: Latest written LSN by tier
panels.description: Most recent WAL LSN the server has written for each tier, as a byte offset.

panels.title: Backup verification rate by outcome and tier
panels.description: Rate of base backup verification checks, broken down by outcome and tier.

panels.title: WAL block duration (p50/p95/p99) by path and stage
panels.description: Percentile per-block WAL processing duration on the server, split by `path` (put ingest / get serve) and `stage`.

panels.title: WAL file get duration (p50/p95/p99) by tier
panels.description: Percentile duration of a complete WAL file gRPC get, split by the tier that served it.

panels.title: WAL tier-2 upload duration (p50/p95/p99) by cluster
panels.description: Percentile duration of the tier-2 archival upload to remote storage, per cluster.

panels.title: Tier-2 relay rate by outcome
panels.description: Rate of tier-2 relay attempts after a backup (migration and verification), by outcome.

panels.title: Maintenance run rate by tier and outcome
panels.description: Rate of post-backup maintenance runs (base-snapshot retention and WAL cleanup), by tier and outcome.

panels.title: Queue messages by stream
panels.description: Messages currently held in each NATS JetStream stream of the embedded queue.

panels.title: Queue bytes by stream
panels.description: Bytes currently held in each NATS JetStream stream of the embedded queue.

panels.title: Tier-1 Replication lag (Bytes)
panels.description: Byte distance between the primary's current WAL LSN and the LSN Klio's streaming client has flushed, from CloudNativePG's pg_stat_replication.

panels.title: Tier-1 Replication lag (Seconds)
panels.description: Time between a commit on the primary and Klio's streaming client flushing the corresponding WAL, from CloudNativePG's pg_stat_replication.

panels.title: Tier-2 archival lag (Tier-1 LSN gap)
panels.description: LSN distance between tier 1 (local disk) and tier 2 (remote storage) per cluster. A growing gap means remote archival is falling behind.
